title: Comprehensive Neuro Set 1: Spinal Reflexes (Short Answer)

questions.prompt: Define a "motor unit" and a "motoneuron pool".
questions.modelAnswer: Motor unit: A single motoneuron and all the muscle fibers it innervates. Motoneuron pool: The set of all motoneurons innervating a single muscle.

questions.prompt: Explain the "size principle" regarding the order of motoneuron recruitment.
questions.modelAnswer: Small motoneurons have lower thresholds and fire first; larger motoneurons are recruited as more force is required.

questions.prompt: Which specific muscle fibers provide the force for contraction, and which type of motoneuron innervates them?
questions.modelAnswer: Extrafusal fibers; innervated by α-motoneurons.

questions.prompt: Describe the structural arrangement of muscle spindles relative to extrafusal muscle fibers.
questions.modelAnswer: Muscle spindles are arranged in parallel with extrafusal fibers.

questions.prompt: What type of motoneuron innervates the contractile ends of intrafusal muscle fibers?
questions.modelAnswer: γ-motoneurons.

questions.prompt: Identify the two types of intrafusal fibers found within a muscle spindle.
questions.modelAnswer: Nuclear bag fibers and nuclear chain fibers.

questions.prompt: Distinguish between nuclear bag and nuclear chain fibers in terms of the specific information they detect (dynamic vs static).
questions.modelAnswer: Nuclear bag fibers detect dynamic changes (velocity/rate of change); nuclear chain fibers detect static changes (length).

questions.prompt: Which sensory afferent fiber provides the primary (annulospiral) ending that detects the rate of change in muscle length?
questions.modelAnswer: Group Ia afferents.

questions.prompt: Which sensory afferent fiber provides the secondary (flower-spray) ending that primarily detects static muscle length?
questions.modelAnswer: Group II afferents.

questions.prompt: Explain the physiological purpose of α-γ coactivation during voluntary movement.
questions.modelAnswer: To prevent the muscle spindle from going slack during contraction, thereby maintaining its sensitivity to stretch.

questions.prompt: What is the specific stimulus that initiates the stretch (myotatic) reflex?
questions.modelAnswer: Muscle stretch (lengthening).

questions.prompt: Why is the stretch reflex categorized as a monosynaptic reflex?
questions.modelAnswer: Because the sensory afferent (Ia) synapses directly onto the α-motoneuron without an intervening interneuron.

questions.prompt: Describe the "reciprocal inhibition" that occurs during a stretch reflex.
questions.modelAnswer: While the stretched (homonymous) muscle is stimulated to contract, its antagonistic muscles are inhibited (relaxed).

questions.prompt: How does the Golgi tendon organ differ from the muscle spindle in its anatomical arrangement relative to extrafusal fibers?
questions.modelAnswer: Golgi tendon organs are arranged in series with extrafusal fibers.

questions.prompt: Which group of sensory afferent fibers is activated by the Golgi tendon organ?
questions.modelAnswer: Group Ib afferents.

questions.prompt: Describe the sequence of events in the Golgi tendon reflex (inverse myotatic reflex) following a strong muscle contraction.
questions.modelAnswer: Strong contraction stretches the tendon → Ib afferents activate inhibitory interneurons → α-motoneurons are inhibited → the muscle relaxes.

questions.prompt: How many synapses are present in the reflex arc of the Golgi tendon reflex?
questions.modelAnswer: Two (disynaptic).

questions.prompt: Define the "clasp-knife reflex" and identify the pathology it typically suggests.
questions.modelAnswer: A sudden decrease in resistance to passive stretch when tension activates the Golgi tendon reflex; suggests corticospinal tract disease (upper motor neuron lesion).

questions.prompt: What is the typical stimulus for the flexor-withdrawal reflex?
questions.modelAnswer: Pain, temperature, or a noxious stimulus.

questions.prompt: Explain the "crossed-extension reflex" that occurs simultaneously with the flexor-withdrawal reflex.
questions.modelAnswer: The ipsilateral limb flexes (withdraws) while the contralateral limb extends to maintain balance.

questions.prompt: Define "recurrent inhibition" and name the specific inhibitory interneuron involved in this process.
questions.modelAnswer: Motoneurons send collaterals to Renshaw cells, which then provide feedback inhibition to that same motoneuron.

questions.prompt: Which inhibitory neurotransmitter is released by Renshaw cells?
questions.modelAnswer: Glycine.

questions.prompt: Contrast "convergence" and "divergence" as they apply to the spinal organization of motor systems.
questions.modelAnswer: Convergence: multiple inputs onto a single neuron. Divergence: a single neuron projecting to multiple targets.

questions.prompt: How do increases in γ-motoneuron activity specifically change the sensitivity of the stretch reflex?
questions.modelAnswer: It increases sensitivity by causing the intrafusal fibers to contract/stiffen, making them more responsive to stretch.

questions.prompt: Define "skeletal muscle tone" in the context of the stretch reflex.
questions.modelAnswer: The resistance to passive stretch produced by continuous, low-level reflex contraction of muscles.
